name: Congenital Stationary Night Blindness

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Electroretinographic Criteria for CSNB

criteria.description: Congenital onset of impaired night vision (nyctalopia) without progression
Characteristic abnormal electroretinogram (ERG) showing absent or reduced rod responses with normal cone responses
Normal fundoscopic examination without retinal degeneration
Positive family history consistent with autosomal recessive or X-linked inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital nyctalopia with characteristic ERG abnormalities
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can confirm diagnosis but is not mandatory

pathognomonic.symptomName: Non-progressive visual impairment under low light conditions

common.symptomName: Reduced visual acuity in dim lighting

imaging: Electroretinogram (ERG) showing absent or severely reduced rod responses with preserved cone responses
genetic: Mutations in NYX, GRM6, TRPM1, CACNA1F, and other genes associated with CSNB
other: Family history consistent with autosomal recessive or X-linked inheritance patterns

distinguishingFeatures: Progressive night blindness with retinal degeneration
Characteristic bone-spicule pigmentation on fundus exam
Photophobia and nystagmus present from birth
Severely reduced cone function on ERG

redFlags: Fundus abnormalities suggestive of retinal degeneration
references: Dryja TP et al. Congenital stationary night blindness: clinical and molecular genetics. Ophthalmology. 2005.
Zeitz C, et al. Congenital stationary night blindness: an analysis and update of genotype-phenotype correlations and pathogenic mechanisms. Prog Retin Eye Res. 2015.
